problem: Embodied navigation agents rely on partial egocentric observations and incremental maps, causing meandering exploration; MLLMs reason well semantically but cannot regress precise coordinates, and prior global-map methods are task-specific, trained, or need dense pre-built scene models.
motivation: Humans plan on a map first (reason globally) then act locally. If a top-down map is available, an MLLM can perform commonsense reasoning about where the goal is, while a deterministic planner handles control, giving a unified zero-shot solution across goal types.
key_idea: Turn navigation into discrete global reasoning: an MLLM picks a room and then a Poisson-disk candidate node on a top-down map (one-off), and a deterministic A*+VFH* planner with detector/MobileSAM verification executes it.
insight: MLLMs fail at coordinate regression but succeed at discrete selection: direct coordinate prediction gives SR 12.3, single-stage node selection 44.5, and coarse-to-fine room-then-node selection 55.1 (Seed-1.6-Thinking, HM3D ObjNav). Reasoning strength matters (Qwen2.5-7B-VL 41.3 SR vs Gemini-2.5-Pro 55.8), and a discriminator ensemble of two MLLMs adds further gains (57.9 SR, largest for ImgNav: 40.7 to 47.8). Global one-off planning yields high SPL because the agent walks directly to the target.
method: Room-level localization: wall mask -> EDT -> Otsu-thresholded seeds -> Watershed -> merge small regions; the MLLM sees the numbered room map and picks the room most likely containing the goal (text prompt, or plus goal image for IIN).

Intra-room node selection: Poisson Disk Sampling (radius 0.5 m) over navigable area gives candidate nodes; nodes in the chosen room are drawn on a cropped map and the MLLM picks one node, which becomes p_global.

Local navigation: online occupancy map initialized from the wall mask and updated from RGB-D; A* (EDF as costmap) replans every T steps, and VFH* follows short-term waypoints; a safety check relocates waypoints falling in occupied cells.

Target verification: on reaching a first proximity threshold, run a detector; otherwise approach closer, then do a 360° scan; on detection MobileSAM mask + depth back-projection gives the 3D centroid to walk to and then stop.
Model ensemble: two GR units (Seed-1.6-Thinking and Gemini-2.5-Pro) each propose a p_global; a GPT-5 discriminator compares the two annotated crops and picks the more plausible and accessible one.
Unified goal handling: the same pipeline handles object-category, instance-image and text-description goals by changing only the prompt and detector query.

setting.backbone: Seed-1.6-thinking + Gemini-2.5-Pro (global reasoning, frozen), GPT-5 (discriminator, frozen); pretrained object detector + MobileSAM; A*/VFH* planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus pose and a pre-built global top-down 2D map
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 30°, stop
setting.privileged: Global top-down 2D map of the environment (with furniture layout) available before navigation; agent pose localized on map

numbers_note: The paper does not state the split explicitly (HM3D 2022 ObjNav challenge, 2023 ImageNav, TextNav following PSL); 'val' is assumed. Ablation single-model rows (Table 3) also give ImgNav (Seed 40.2/25.2, Gemini 40.7/25.6) and TextNav (Seed 30.1/19.0, Gemini 37.2/22.8) results.
results: ReasonNavi ensemble gets 57.9 SR / 31.4 SPL on HM3D ObjNav, highest SPL among all methods (beating VLFM 30.4 SPL and Trihelper 56.5 SR), and 38.8 SR / 24.3 SPL on TextNav versus UniGoal 20.2 / 11.4. On ImgNav it has best SPL (30.4) but lower SR (47.8) than UniGoal (60.2) and IEVE (70.2).
limitations: Requires a clean pre-built global top-down map, which may be unavailable in real deployments
One-off reasoning: no use of local observations to correct a wrong global plan
Objects with ambiguous top-down appearance (clothes, TV) are hard for the MLLM to locate; no real-robot experiments
